data.title: UI specification for the landing page
body: # UI specification for the landing page
- **Stack:** Next.js (App Router) + Tailwind + Motion, hosted on Vercel, separate repository ([ADR-008](DOC-11))
- **Rests on:** [the visual direction](DOC-18), [the copy](DOC-25), [the structure](DOC-51)
- **Prototype:** the artifact "kadence — landing page prototype"
## 1. Grid and rhythm
container     1120 px max · padding 24 px (mob.) / 40 px (desktop)
columns       12 · gap 24 px
text measure  62–68 characters — no paragraph is wider
vertical      section 96 px (mob. 64) top and bottom; 32 px between blocks inside
divider       a 1 px hairline across the full container width, not a card
**Spacing scale** (multiples of 8, one for the whole site): 4 · 8 · 12 · 16 · 24 · 32 · 48 · 64 · 96 · 128.
**Breakpoints:** 390 (base, mobile-first) · 768 · 1024 · 1280.
Two-column sections (hero, demo, "how it works") fold into one column at 768. The terminal block is never scaled below a 12.5 px font — it gets its own horizontal scroll instead.
## 2. Section layout
| # | Section | Desktop | Mobile | Main element |
| 0 | Nav | sticky, 56 px tall, `backdrop-blur` background, hairline below after 40 px of scroll | logo + "Docs · GitHub" | the mark `\|:` + wordmark |
| 1 | Hero | 6/6: text and CTA on the left, `task show --json` on the right — what the agent reads | stack: H1 → sub → CTA → terminal | the install command with copy |
| 2 | Demo | full width, 16:9 video max 880 px, centred | full width, 16 px padding | `<video>` with a poster |
| 3 | Problem → change | three blocks 4/4/4, divided by hairlines | stack | the middle block ("agitate") is visually heavier |
| 4 | Why events, not files | 4/4/4 cards — **the only place with cards on the page** | stack | below them, the line about state always being recomputable |
| 5 | Merge proof | numbers 7 columns, text 5 | numbers in a 2×2 grid | `8 396` as the largest number on the page |
| 6 | How it works | steps 7 columns, the `.kadence/` tree 5 | stack | the monospaced tree |
| 7 | Cost of ownership | full-width table, risk reducers in three columns | table → list of pairs | the "Licence · MIT" line |
| 8 | For agents | 5 columns of text, 7 of code | stack, code first | the code block with `--json` |
| 9 | Honest status | three sub-blocks, narrower measure (56 characters) | stack | the 20-minute hook at the end |
| 10 | FAQ + repeat CTA | FAQ 7 columns, CTA 5 — sticky within the section | stack, CTA after the FAQ | the same install command |
| 11 | Footer | four columns of links | two columns | the mark once more, small |

**The demo comes second — immediately under the hero.** The YC advice for dev tools is literal: show the product in the first screen or right below it, not buried under paragraphs. The video poster is visible without a click, so the "first screen" effectively holds both the command and the result.
## 3. Components and states
### Copy button (main CTA)
| State | Appearance | Detail |
| Rest | `--rule-strong` border, `--paper` background, `copy` label in the accent | `pointer` cursor over the whole block |
| Hover | the border darkens to `--accent`, the background unchanged | 120 ms |
| Focus | 2 px `--accent` outline, 2 px offset | visible from the keyboard, not only on hover |
| Pressed | the label changes to `copied` | 2 s, then back; `aria-live="polite"` |
| Failure | the label reads `press ⌘C` and the text is selected | when `navigator.clipboard` is unavailable |
### Demo video
- `poster` — the final frame with the number, WebP; `preload="none"`, `playsinline`, muted, **no autoplay**
- The `Play the 40-second demo` button — not "Watch video": the number in the label answers "how long will this take"
- Under the player — the line "No cuts. This is the whole loop." and a link to a text version of the same commands for those who do not watch video
- Formats: WebM (VP9) with an MP4 (H.264) fallback, both ≤ 1080p, ≤ 4 MB
- No captions needed — there is no sound; but `aria-label` describes what is shown
### FAQ
`<details>`/`<summary>` — native, works without JS, indexable. The first item is open by default. `FAQPage` schema.org markup.
### The "cost of ownership" table
`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, the right column aligned on the digit. On mobile it turns into a list of "label — value" pairs rather than scrolling.
## 4. Motion
There is freedom, but it is spent where the motion means something. One rule: **an animation either explains causality, or it does not exist.**
| What | Trigger | Duration | Curve | Why |
| The number `1.6h per point` in the hero | load, delayed 400 ms after the output | 260 ms | `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)` | shows that the number is **printed**, not typed in |
| Section reveal | IntersectionObserver, threshold 0.15 | 320 ms | the same | `opacity` 0→1, `translateY` 8→0. Only `transform` and `opacity` |
| Nav hairline | scroll > 40 px | 160 ms | `ease-out` | the boundary between page and bar |
| Hover on the CTA and links | hover | 120 ms | `ease-out` | |
| Board frames in section 4 | hover on a card | 200 ms | `ease-out` | a column highlight, not movement |
**What is absent:** scroll-jacking, parallax, counters that run up, text that types itself, carousels, cursor effects, particles.

**The reason is not taste.** CrUX data for March 2026: only 55% of sites are "good" on LCP/INP/CLS, and JS scroll animations are among the main causes of failure. A page that sells an 80 ms start cannot afford a 300 ms INP.
**`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`** turns off everything in the table, the number's appearance included: it is simply already there.

**The page at rest is fully readable.** The reveals are built so that without JS everything is visible straight away — the class that hides an element is set by script, and only if IntersectionObserver is available.
## 5. Performance budget
| Metric | Target | How we hold it |
| LCP | < 1.2 s | the LCP element is the H1, i.e. text. The heading font is `preload`, `font-display: swap` |
| INP | < 100 ms | there are two handlers on the page: copy and play |
| CLS | 0 | the video and the poster have a fixed `aspect-ratio`; the fonts have `size-adjust` in the fallback |
| JS on the first screen | < 30 KB | Motion is imported dynamically and only for sections below the fold |
| Total weight of the first screen | < 120 KB | without the video — it is `preload="none"` |
Next.js works here as a static generator: every section is a Server Component, with only two client islands (the copy button, the player).
## 6. Accessibility
- Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for all text in both themes; terminal blocks are checked separately
- Focus visible on every interactive element, the tab order matching the visual one
- One `<h1>`, then levels with no gaps
- Terminal blocks are `<pre>` with an `aria-label` describing the content
- The theme follows the system; there is no switch — a spare element and a spare state
- The CTA is reachable by keyboard two Tabs from the top of the page
## 7. SEO and metadata
title        kadence — shared context for your team and your agents   (54 characters)
description  Tasks, their history and the time they took live in your git repo as an
append-only journal. Your team and your agents read the same thing.
og:image     1200×630, the sprint close output on the paper ground, the number in ochre
twitter:card summary_large_image
schema       SoftwareApplication + FAQPage
One `<h1>`. URLs: `/`, `/docs`, `/compare/backlog-md`, `/talk`. Canonical links to `https://kadence.guru` (the domain was registered 2026-09-13; `kadence.tools` was the plan).

**The target queries are not the name.** The name "kadence" in organic search belongs to the WordPress builder Kadence WP (see section 11 of [the visual direction](DOC-18)). So the page is optimised for `git task tracker`, `sprint velocity cli`, `tasks in git repo`, `backlog.md alternative`, and no traffic on the name is planned at all.
## 8. Structure of the site repository
kadence-site/
|- app/
|  |- layout.tsx            fonts, metadata, theme
|  |- page.tsx              assembling the sections
|  `- opengraph-image.tsx   og generated from the same tokens
|- components/
|  |- sections/             Hero, Demo, Problem, ThreeThings, MergeProof,
|  |                        HowItWorks, Cost, Agents, Honest, Faq, Footer
|  |- CopyCommand.tsx       client island
|  |- DemoPlayer.tsx        client island
|  `- Terminal.tsx          server-side, just a <pre>
|- content/
|  |- facts.json            every number + a source field on each (ADR-008)
|  `- copy.ts               section texts in one place
|- public/
|  |- demo.webm · demo.mp4 · demo-poster.webp
|  `- favicon
`- styles/tokens.css        colour and typography tokens
`content/facts.json` is the one place where `32 KB`, `80 ms`, `8,396`, `15%`, `1.6h per point` live. No number is written into JSX by hand.
## 9. What to check before publishing
- [ ] Lighthouse ≥ 95 on all four on a throttled mobile profile
- [ ] CLS = 0 on a slow network — the poster and the video have their size before loading
- [ ] The page reads with JS disabled: everything is visible except the copy button
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion` turns off every reveal
- [ ] Every number on the page is in `facts.json` and has a source
- [ ] Checked at 390 px and at 1440 px, in the light and the dark theme
- [ ] The demo re-recorded after the last change in `src/tui/`
